source: FAO / Royal University of Agriculture (RUA) / Australian Government AusAID, coconut beetle (leaf beetle / hispine beetle, ត្មាត / ខ្មៅមាល់អាសេកូដ program) trifold pest-control leaflet, published 2005
text:
The coconut hispid leaf beetle (locally referred to in this leaflet in connection with the parasitic wasp program targeting it) is a major pest of coconut palms (ដើមដូង) in Cambodia. Its larvae and adults feed on the young, unopened leaflets at the crown of the palm, scraping the leaf tissue as the leaf unfolds.

Damage caused by the beetle includes: leaves turning brown, scorched-looking, and drying out prematurely; reduced flowering and fruit set, which lowers coconut yield; a visibly damaged, unattractive palm canopy; and a general decline in the tree's vigor and its usefulness to farmers for both fruit and by-product production.

Because damage concentrates in the growing crown of the palm, heavily infested trees can suffer repeated damage to each new leaf as it emerges, compounding yield loss over successive seasons if the pest is not controlled.
